messages:
jane_sales: FYI — prospect (global bank) asked if we can do an air-gapped deployment with a quarterly upgrade cadence instead of monthly. They also want signed, quantized bundles and delta patching. Can SE + security confirm feasibility?

mike_se: @jane_sales short answer: yes, but tradeoffs. Quarterly upgrades are fine for security-minded customers but we need to extend patch support windows and change default fallback policies.

ana_security: typo: @mike_se @jane_sales (I’m ana_security) — quarterly cadence ok but require: SBOM, signed artifacts (HSM/KMS), reproducible build hashes, and a formal vulnerability SLA in contract. Also need a secure process for offline key provisioning.

mike_se: Agree. Practically: we can provide a signed tar.gz that includes quantized model shards + runtime. Typical bundle size for our quantized 4-bit LLaMA-variant is ~13.2GB. Install flow would be: scp -> verify signature -> run ./install.sh --offline.

jane_sales: They specifically called out delta updates (small patches between quarters). Is that supported? They don’t want to redeliver 13GB every time.

tim_ops: We have a delta patch mechanism but it’s currently alpha for quantized weights. We can emit patch packs with changed chunks; customers need our delta client to apply. Ops note: patch packs require the same build provenance (same base bundle hash). If we do quarterly, patch cadence can be monthly but only if customer runs our delta client.

ana_security: Also required: offline attestation log for each applied patch, and signed rollout metadata. We should provide a step-by-step: verify signature -> verify sbom -> run attestation -> apply.

mike_se: Example command snippet we give in docs:

```
# verify signature
./redwood-sign-verify --artifact redwood-bundle-v1.tar.gz --pubkey bank-pub.pem
# apply delta
./redwood-delta-client apply delta-pack-2026-05.patch
```

jane_sales: Good. Pricing question from PO — does air-gapped + quarterly cadence change pricing vs regular private? They asked about yearly maintenance and extended patch windows.

mike_se: Pricing basics: base private license + delivery fee for air-gap packaging + per-quarter maintenance if they want us to produce deltas and signed bundles. Suggest: 10% uplift for airgap + optional SLA/patching retainer. Exact numbers require commercial to finalize.

ana_security: For contracts, add clause: customer to provide a secured channel (sftp with MFA, or physical USB via courier) for artifact delivery and for key exchange. Also list supported OS images and kernel versions — we have a compatibility matrix to attach.

tim_ops: One operational blocker: our current installer expects systemd on Linux. If customer runs a strict appliance (no systemd) we need ~2 weeks eng time to make a non-systemd installer. Flagging that as potential delay.

jane_sales: Noted — customer uses a hardened minimal RHEL image with systemd disabled by default. I'll surface the ~2 week engineering delta.

mike_se: Final notes: we can enable quantized bundles to reduce size and cost, but some model quality/regression testing is required before signing. Recommend a short POC: ship bundle -> customer runs smoke tests -> we ship first delta. POC checklist: SBOM, signing key exchange, test prompts, installer runbook.

ana_security: I'll draft answers for their security questionnaire and include sample attestation logs and SBOM. ETA EOD tomorrow.

deploy-bot: build 9852 passed for redwood-bundles (quantized) — artifacts available at internal-artifacts.example.com/builds/9852 (signed). :white_check_mark:

jane_sales: Perfect — thanks everyone. I'll update the customer and follow up with contract asks and the POC checklist. :thumbsup:
